svg.title: Downunder Voices Cartoon of the Day — Santa came early. The camp chairs came earlier.
svg.desc: Pen-and-ink editorial cartoon of an Adelaide street on Christmas pageant day under grey, hatched clouds, with Victorian shopfronts and iron lace verandahs on the left, a sandstone building with a clock tower on the right, plane trees and bunting across the road. A float shaped like a sleigh piled with presents carries a waving Father Christmas past a crowd behind a barrier. In the foreground a fictional family waits on the footpath: a woman under an umbrella, a child in a beanie waving a little flag, and a man in a cap sitting in a camp chair with a thermos cup, pointing at a row of four empty folding chairs roped together beside a sign reading Reserved, Back soon, with cobwebs and a small spider on them. He says: We got here at dawn. Those chairs have been here since Tuesday. Caption: Santa came early. The camp chairs came earlier.
svg.text: DOWNUNDER VOICES — CARTOON OF THE DAY

g.text: WE GOT HERE AT DAWN. THOSE
CHAIRS HAVE BEEN HERE SINCE TUESDAY.

svg.text: SANTA CAME EARLY. THE CAMP CHAIRS CAME EARLIER.
Source: ABC News, 14 November 2026 — An estimated 335,000 people lined the route of Adelaide’s Christmas pageant under grey skies.
